traits.note: FNA vol. 27, Grimmiaceae (Hastings and Ochyra; efloras, read 2026-11-05): plants acrocarpous or cladocarpous, olivaceous to blackish green, in rigid cushions, tufts, mats or patches; leaves erect and tightly appressed to crisped when dry, spreading when wet, typically with a hyaline awn; capsule usually erect. Most species are xerophytes colonising bare, dry, exposed rock and stones as dark cushions; few on soil, few epiphytes. Built surfaces (old mortar, walls) as for the genera below.
